newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends firm in third straight closing high.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends firm in third straight closing high.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 ends slightly firmer, marking third
** UK trade figures meet market expectations and
** B.A.T up on favourable U.S. tobacco court ruling.
"Sterling is still strong and it looks like interest rates are probably going to rise soon, but that hasn't unnerved the market," he said.
"Most institutions aren't in the market and those that are can't afford to sell," added another who was looking for a test of the 4,100 level in early January.
The UK November trade figures, broadly in line with market expectations, failed to generate interest, dealers said.
"The idea today is to get out the door as quickly as possible," a dealer said.
Among individual stocks, shares in B.A.T Industries climbed 4p to 482-1/2p after a Missouri court ruled in its favour by granting its motion to be dismissed from a U.S. tobacco suit.

Shares in Northern Electric, which resumed trading today after being suspended yesterday, fell 4p to 637p after losing the UK Takeover Panel last night gave the green light to CalEnergy's CE.L controversial 782 million stg bid to go through.
